properties.name: pqs:context

The two JSON sites (aoi puzzle.json:67, puzzles.json:85) are catalog summaries documenti

components.name: weak password hash

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The practice is real: puzzle passwords are derived from candidate answers by single fast digests — gsmg's stated convention password = sha256(X) (oracle.py:169, and phase2_password = sha256(b"causality") at :212, a known-answer vector), plus MD5-chain EvpKDF (:232, arweave:184) stretching those passwords into AES keys. The JSON sites (gsmg pipeline-stages.json:5, puzzle.json:49, puzzles.json:652) document this convention. None of it is credential storage; it is key derivation for decrypting puzz

components.name: SHA-1

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Peter Todd's hash-collision bounty oracle: SHA-1 is the puzzle TARGET itself — the oracle computes SHA-1 digests of candidate data (:98 helper) and tests candidate pairs for collisions (:160). SHA-1 use is intrinsic to the bounty being solved, not a free choice; still a real, quantum-unsafe (collision-broken) algorithm use in first-party code.

components.name: 3DES

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency capability: pycryptodome is declared in tools/requirements.txt and ships Crypto.Cipher.DES3, so the shipped environment can do 3DES. No first-party DES3 call site exists anywhere in the repo (grep for Crypto imports shows only Cipher.AES and Crypto.Hash usages). Presence is the inventory question here; the application never calls it. 3DES is broken independently of quantum computing.

components.name: EVP_BytesToKey

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The pipeline-stages.json edge documents a real, implemented scheme: OpenSSL "Salted__" AES-256-CBC blobs whose key+IV come from EVP_BytesToKey with a selectable digest — SHA-256 for phases 2/3 and MD5 for the Cosmic Duality blob (the historical CryptoJS/openssl enc behavior). The Python implementation is gsmg oracle.py evp_bytes_to_key() (:89-101, md5 chain at :232) and the engines' evpkdf() (MD5, 10000 iterations — the crypto-js #293 quirk). Single-round/MD5-digest EVP_BytesToKey is a weak KDF,

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA512 is the workhorse of BIP32/BIP39 derivation here: master-key derivation hmac.new(b"Bitcoin seed", seed, sha512) and child-key derivation hmac.new(c, data, sha512) across blm/guntis/corey/veteranhodl oracles and the engines (bip39pass_eth, bip39pass_stream, lib/bip39_multipath). Same construction the GPU engines implement natively (engines/bip39_passphrase_engine.cu). HMAC-SHA512 is quantum-safe against key recovery (Grover only) — this is the strong end of the repo's inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-512 plays two roles: the Arweave series' key stretching (sha512^11513 chains: arweave oracles :173-175, engines/pzl3_host.py:49-51, engines/arweave_var_host.py:58-60, genesis candidates.py:229 lambda) and the inner hash of every BIP32 HMAC (veteranhodl:165 seed-version hmac, blm/guntis/corey/veteranhodl/engines BIP32 chains). The stretch chain is the puzzle's published scheme (also reproduced on GPU in engines/*.cu). SHA-512 meets CNSA 2.0 — strong end of the inventory; quantum exposure is G

components.name: AES-256
TLS

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency capability: the requests library bundles a TLS client (urllib3/OpenSSL). No live HTTPS session exists in the tree — tls_sessions found no session setup and no requests.get/post call sites — so this is capability-only, no first-party TLS configuration to assess (no cipher lists, no verify=False anywhere). Grading defaults is therefore not possible from this tree; the shipped requests version determines what TLS the tools WOULD use if extended.

components.name: pycryptodome

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PyCryptodome is the repo's workhorse provider: Crypto.Cipher.AES (AES-256-CBC decrypt in gsmg/path-to-greatness oracles), Crypto.Hash.keccak (Ethereum address derivation in arweave-11 tools, guntis sweep_paths, teikhos, engines/bip39pass_eth), Crypto.Hash.RIPEMD160 (address HASH160 fallback in ~8 oracles). Declared unpinned in tools/requirements.txt, so the shipped version decides available primitives; the version is not recorded anywhere in the tree.

components.name: ecdsa

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The pure-python ecdsa library performs all CPU-side secp256k1 operations in the oracle tools: SigningKey.from_string/from_secret_exponent(SECP256k1) for pubkey derivation before HASH160 (keir, derive.py, gsmg, rushwallet, zden, andy-bauch, veteranhodl, corey...). Pure-python ECDSA is slow but algorithmically standard secp256k1 ECDSA — Shor-vulnerable like all EC cryptography; the faster libsecp256k1 path (coincurve) is used by the engines and some sweep tools.

components.name: requests

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HTTP client dependency; bundles the TLS transport capability (see the TLS object). No call sites in the tree — the tools are deliberately offline (docstrings: "no network", funds verified on-chain by humans). Present in the dependency inventory because it ships and would carry TLS defaults if used.
